chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man afflicted with smallpox who was struck by janabah, and he said:
“If he became junub himself, then let him perform ghusl, and if he had a nocturnal emission, then let him perform tayammum.”

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became junub through his own act
key_terms.احْتَلَمَ: experienced a nocturnal emission in sleep
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring purification

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person with smallpox who becomes junub?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity for a person afflicted with smallpox who enters a state of janabah. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام distinguishes between janabah caused directly by one’s act and janabah caused by nocturnal emission, assigning ghusl in the first case and tayammum in the second.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.220 - It was asked of Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a man with smallpox who became junub (ritually impure due to sexual discharge).
Imam (as) said:
'If he became junub (through intercourse), he should perform ghusl, but if he had a nocturnal emission (i.e., he experienced it while sleeping), he should perform tayammum.'.
